title: Signal spread from many towers
prompt:
Return the minutes until signal from every tower "S" covers all open "." cells of a grid, spreading one cell up, down, left or right per minute, or -1 if it never does.

- grid is a list of equal-length strings with 1 to 200 rows and 1 to 200 columns; "#" cells block signal and never need coverage.
- All towers start covered at minute 0 and spread at the same time.
- Return 0 when there is no "." cell. With no towers but at least one "." cell, return -1.
hints: Running a separate search from each tower and taking the minimum per cell works but repeats a lot of effort.
Put every tower into one breadth-first search queue at distance 0, as if they all hang off a single invisible super-source.
Each cell's distance is the minute it is first covered. The largest distance assigned is the answer, and any "." left uncovered means -1.

solution.explanation: Seeding one breadth-first search with every tower at distance 0 makes each cell's distance its minute of first coverage from the nearest tower. Cells are dequeued in nondecreasing distance, so the last distance assigned is the overall finish time. Counting uncovered "." cells detects the impossible case.

complexity.notes: Each cell enters the queue at most once. One BFS per tower would cost O(towers · rows · cols).

followUps: Some cells now slow the signal down, taking 2 minutes to cross instead of 1. What changes in the search?
